newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia mulling new proposal for Fokker rescue.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia mulling new proposal for Fokker rescue.

text.p: The Malaysian government is considering a new set of proposals for the rescue of bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker, Malaysian newspapers reported on Friday.

Abdul Rashid Hussain, a director of the government's investment arm Khazanah Holdings Bhd, said a proposal submitted by a group of Dutch investors was rejected two weeks ago, the Business Times newspaper said.

"Khazanah could not accept their demands. The original people who brought the deal to us are no longer the key players. There is now greater involvement on a government-to-government level," the newspaper quoted Abdul Rashid as telling reporters on Thursday.
Khazanah officials could not be reached on Friday for comment.
Abdul Rashid said Khazanah was considering the new proposal, which he did not detail, with help from "experts around the world".
"Upon completion of this study, we will decide whether or not to become an investor," the Sun newspaper quoted him as saying.
Fokker was declared bankrupt a year ago after majority shareholder Daimler Benz AG of Germany said it would no longer bear Fokker's huge losses.
Malaysia is one in a string of potential suitors. Other possible saviours have been Canadians, Koreans and Russians, and rumours of fresh interest crop up constantly.
This week, Saudi Arabian Prince al-Waleed bin Talal, nephew of King Fahd, has been touted as a possible white knight.
